units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Yes, but my dear, good child--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Then I should be glad to go to town. It's very lonely out here; you know yourself, sir, what it is to be alone in the world. And I can assure you I'm both quick and willing. Don't you know of any such place for me, sir?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: I? No, certainly not.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: But, dear, dear Sir, do remember me if--
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Rising.
Yes, yes, certainly, Miss Engstrand.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: For if I--
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Will you be so good as to tell your mistress I am here?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I will, at once, sir.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: She goes out to the left.
Paces the room two or three times, stands a moment in the background with his hands behind his back, and looks out over the garden.
Then he returns to the table, takes up a book, and looks at the title-page; starts, and looks at several books.
Ha--indeed!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: MRS. ALVING enters by the door on the left; she is followed by REGINA, who immediately goes out by the first door on the right.
Holds out her hand.
Welcome, my dear Pastor.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: How do you do, Mrs. Alving? Here I am as I promised.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Always punctual to the minute.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: You may believe it was not so easy for me to get away. With all the Boards and Committees I belong to--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: That makes it all the kinder of you to come so early. Now we can get through our business before dinner. But where is your portmanteau?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Quickly.
I left it down at the inn. I shall sleep there to-night.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Suppressing a smile.
Are you really not to be persuaded, even now, to pass the night under my roof?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No, no, Mrs. Alving; many thanks. I shall stay at the inn, as usual. It is so conveniently near the landing-stage.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well, you must have your own way. But I really should have thought we two old people--
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Now you are making fun of me. Ah, you're naturally in great spirits to-day--what with to-morrow's festival and Oswald's return.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes; you can think what a delight it is to me! It's more than two years since he was home last. And now he has promised to stay with me all the winter.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Has he really? That is very nice and dutiful of him. For I can well believe that life in Rome and Paris has very different attractions from any we can offer here.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Ah, but here he has his mother, you see. My own darling boy--he hasn't forgotten his old mother!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: It would be grievous indeed, if absence and absorption in art and that sort of thing were to blunt his natural feelings.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, you may well say so. But there's nothing of that sort to fear with him. I'm quite curious to see whether you know him again. He'll be down presently; he's upstairs just now, resting a little on the sofa. But do sit down, my dear Pastor.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Thank you. Are you quite at liberty--?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Certainly.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: She sits by the table.
Very well. Then let me show you--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: He goes to the chair where his travelling-bag lies, takes out a packet of papers, sits down on the opposite side of the table, and tries to find a clear space for the papers.
Now, to begin with, here is--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Breaking off.
Tell me, Mrs. Alving, how do these books come to be here?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: These books? They are books I am reading.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Do you read this sort of literature?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Certainly I do.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Do you feel better or happier for such reading?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I feel, so to speak, more secure.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: That is strange. How do you mean?
units.name: MANDERS
